title: Pensacola Bay Bluffs
sequence: Pensacola · US 90 at the south end of Scenic Highway
description: Pensacola saves its best angle on the bay for the drive out of town. Take Scenic Highway north. The houses break, the ground rises and Escambia Bay flashes between the trees below the passenger window. Give the bluffs a second look from a public overlook. The road itself is narrow in places, and those glimpses go by quickly.
survey: Neighborhood driveways open directly onto US 90. Choose a signed public access for a photo and check the grade before taking a low splitter down a ramp.

title: Barrier Island Highway
sequence: Cocoa Beach at the SR 520 causeway
description: One strip of land holds this whole drive together. Start on the barrier island north of Sebastian Inlet and trace A1A through Melbourne Beach. The quiet dune line gives way to surf shops and crosswalks as Cocoa Beach comes into range. Leave the cars at a beach access for the photograph. The ocean looks very different from the other side of those dunes.
survey: Allow extra time through the beach towns. Surf breaks and launches can fill public lots. Use paved access and keep the car off beach sand.

title: Coquina Coast
sequence: South end of Gulf Drive at Coquina Beach
description: Start with beach umbrellas at Coquina and roll north into Bradenton Beach. The Gulf Dr stretch is short enough for the whole crew to make the same lunch reservation, and slow enough for someone on the sidewalk to hear each car arrive. Park once near Bridge Street and finish the afternoon on foot.
survey: Frequent crosswalks, cyclists and trolley stops. Parking fills on beach weekends. This is a short social Cruise.

title: Cross Creek Passage
description: The first act is open country. Then CR 325 slips into Cross Creek, where a narrow piece of land separates Orange Lake from Lochloosa Lake. Turn down the radio here. Spanish moss, fishing boats and the old Rawlings homestead give this piece of Florida a voice all its own. The last miles unwind north toward Rochelle.
survey: Two-lane county road with private drives and little shoulder. The Rawlings site is an optional parked stop. Save the route before the rural section.

title: Upper Keys Passage
description: The first time the mangroves open, you understand why someone built a highway out here. Take US 1 through Tavernier and Islamorada, trading island streets for flashes of pale water between the keys. Let the crew regroup on land. The best part is watching the horizon get wider with every crossing.
survey: One main highway serves the islands. Allow for bridge queues, turning traffic and holiday congestion. Fuel and regroup in town before the longer Middle Keys leg.

title: Guana Coast
description: Leave the Vilano junction with the Atlantic on your right. Past the houses, the dunes rise and the Guana reserve takes over the west side of A1A. There are miles where the sound gives away the ocean before you can see it. Leave time for a dune walkover. That is where the full width of this coast comes into view.
survey: Use the signed reserve lots for beach stops. Look for people crossing A1A and for sand along the pavement after wind or storms.

title: Venice Tamiami
description: Follow the old Tamiami line northwest out of North Port. Venice arrives gradually, first in the palms and broad boulevards, then in the change to the original business route. Venice Avenue is the finish. Park the cars and take the last part of the evening to the beach on foot or as a separate trip.
survey: This is an urban Gulf Coast Cruise with traffic signals. Beach and jetty photography requires a separate stop beyond the mapped finish.

title: Palma Sola Crossing
sequence: East Bay Drive on Anna Maria Island
description: On Manatee Avenue, suburban Bradenton ends almost in a single frame. Suddenly there are paddlers beside the road and water on both sides of the car. The Palma Sola crossing is a short entrance to the island with a long view. Roll it once with the windows down, then find a paved space for the lineup.
survey: Beach traffic and the island bridge can back up. Sand and soft edges are common beside the causeway. Scout a paved parking entrance before pulling off.

title: Green Mountain Overlook
description: West of Lake Apopka the ground starts doing something unexpected. The road rises, tips away and rises again through Montverde and Ferndale. Park at the Green Mountain overlook and take the short walk for the view over the basin. Back at the wheel, the sequence of crests carries the drive into Astatula.
survey: Rolling two-lane roads attract cyclists. Sightlines shorten over the crests. The overlook is optional and the viewing platform is reached on foot.

title: Citrus Ridge
description: Frostproof starts this drive with citrus country and a road that keeps lifting just enough to show you another lake. Follow SR 17 through Babson Park and Lake Wales, then stay with Scenic Highway as it threads the ridge towns north. Each town interrupts the rhythm for a few blocks. The hills pick it right back up.
survey: Village limits, school traffic and farm entrances break up the open sections. Bok Tower Gardens is a separate excursion near Lake Wales. Leave time for its grounds if you add it.

title: Courtney Campbell Crossing
description: Tampa falls away in the mirrors and the causeway lays a thin line across Old Tampa Bay. The whole point of this westbound crossing is the sky. On a clear evening the water holds the light long after the buildings on shore go dark. Make the photo stop at a designated access before or after the span.
survey: Wind is more noticeable on the exposed bridge. Check FL511 before departure and allow for Tampa–Clearwater commuter traffic. Stopping on the span is unsuitable.

title: Bartram River Road
sequence: San Jose Boulevard at the north end of the corridor
description: Take SR 13 north from the Shands Bridge junction and let the St. Johns set the pace. The river disappears behind old oaks and waterside homes, then turns up again exactly where you stopped expecting it. Finish along San Jose Boulevard. The smaller, shaded sections are what you will remember.
survey: Residential entrances and cyclists share the corridor. The route follows the riverbank. Crossing Shands Bridge is a separate drive.

title: Hutchinson Island Passage
sequence: Northeast Ocean Boulevard at Jensen Beach
description: North of Jensen Beach the island stretches into a long ribbon between the Atlantic and the Indian River. Beach accesses tick past until the buildings tighten around Fort Pierce Inlet. Follow Seaway Drive back toward the mainland for the finish. Bring the camera out at a signed waterfront lot while the light is still on the water.
survey: Expect beach crossings and queues around the bridges. Plan any inlet stop before the return to the mainland. The route crosses developed sections.

title: Suncoast Parkway
sequence: Suncoast Parkway north through Pasco and Hernando
description: Trade the junctions on SR 54 for one sustained northbound run. The Suncoast Parkway cuts through pine country with the trail beside it and a much bigger sky than the Tampa departure suggests. Meet the crew at the trailhead, make the drive, then regroup off the parkway at the north end.
survey: Tolled limited-access road. Arrange electronic toll payment and fuel before entering. Use the trailhead access roads for the meetup and finish.

title: Forgotten Coast
description: Eastpoint opens with oyster country. By Carrabelle the boats and working waterfront are right beside the highway. Keep going east and the pines break into broad reaches of tidal water around Ochlockonee Bay. This stretch of the Forgotten Coast rewards a long stop as much as a long drive. Carrabelle is the natural place to make it.
survey: Allow for local traffic through Carrabelle. Services are spaced out on the eastern leg. Low coastal sections can flood after storms. Check fuel and conditions before leaving town.

title: The Ormond Canopy
sequence: Granada Boulevard at North Beach Street
description: Begin by the river in Ormond Beach and follow the trees inland. Along Old Dixie the branches close overhead, then Walter Boardman Lane trades the canopy for marsh light. High Bridge Road delivers you to A1A. This is the wooded and marshland side of the famous Ormond loop, with the ocean waiting at the finish.
survey: Narrow shaded approaches, cyclists and wet leaves call for space. The mapped drive is one way. High Bridge openings can add time.

title: Black Bear Crossing
sequence: SR 40 at Northeast 55th Avenue, Silver Springs
description: East of Silver Springs the storefronts thin out and the pines take over. SR 40 draws a long line through the Ocala forest, with Juniper Springs tucked just off the road. Put it on the itinerary if the crew wants a swim or a photo in the shade. The forest crossing itself stays on pavement.
survey: Fuel in Silver Springs. Expect wildlife and limited places to pull off. Save the route before entering the forest. Juniper Springs has separate access and admission.

title: Lemon Bay Coast
sequence: Placida at the Boca Grande Causeway junction
description: Leave the Boca Grande junction behind and follow the mainland edge of Lemon Bay. Placida Road takes you past marina turns and old fishing neighborhoods before Englewood changes the tempo. Give yourselves time to turn a lunch stop into a walk beside the bay. The beach islands are side trips from this route.
survey: Signals increase around Englewood. The Boca Grande toll bridge is outside this drive. Use designated parking for water access and watch trailer traffic near ramps.

title: 30A Dune Lakes
description: Dune Allen sets the scene, but the dune lakes are the reason to take this stretch of 30A. Salt air and pines trade places through Blue Mountain Beach and Grayton. Then Western Lake opens a strip of sky almost level with the road. Put the cars away for the last photograph. It is worth seeing from the shore.
survey: This western 30A segment ends before central Seaside. Expect bikes, beach crossings and summer queues. Use a public beach or park access for group photos.

title: Flagler Farm Country
description: Turn north on SR 11 and the postcard version of Flagler County disappears. Fields and tree lines stretch away on either side, and Bunnell feels like a destination again when the traffic signals finally come back. This is the paved inland chapter of the Heritage Crossroads district. The coast can wait until the next drive.
survey: Stay on paved SR 11. Some historic side roads in this district have unpaved sections. Expect agricultural vehicles and slow traffic near Bunnell.

title: River of Lakes
sequence: North Woodland Boulevard at International Speedway Boulevard, DeLand
description: Take the old north road out of DeLand. De Leon Springs gives way to fern country, and by Pierson the roadside sheds and fields tell you what this valley grows. Stay on US 17 to Seville. If a photograph of Lake George is the prize, set aside time for a separate trip west to the water.
survey: This leg follows the inland highway. Lake George is a side trip. Allow room for agricultural traffic and check fuel before carrying on beyond Seville.

title: The Broward Beachfront
description: Las Olas puts you on the oceanfront with the city still wide awake. Cruise north past the beachfront cafés, then watch the skyline dip and the lighthouse come into play at Hillsboro Inlet. This is a drive to be seen arriving on. Pick one waterfront meetup and enjoy the rest of Broward from the driver's seat.
survey: Frequent crossings, local parking restrictions and drawbridge queues. Reserve time for parking. Beachside streets are busiest on weekends.

title: Penney Farms Arrival
description: Ease onto the short stretch of SR 16 through Penney Farms. The little community that carries J. C. Penney's name is the whole reason for the drive. Arrange a meetup nearby and do the history and photographs on foot. You can cross this entire territory in the time a longer run takes to warm up.
survey: Short residential heritage Cruise. Keep the group small. Community buildings and residential grounds have their own access rules.

title: Sumter County Lines
description: Take the county road east into Bushnell, then swing north and west toward Lake Panasoffkee. The pleasure here is in the change of scale. An open stretch of pasture narrows into a small-town main road, and just as quickly the horizon widens again. Dade Battlefield makes a worthwhile separate stop near Bushnell.
survey: Watch for farm equipment and freight traffic near US 301. Check the entrance and hours before adding the state park. Lake access requires leaving the main road.

title: Martin Grade
description: Turn west on Martin Highway and the live oaks reach across the centerline until daylight comes through in narrow bands. Beyond their shade, flat pasture opens on both sides. Twelve miles is enough for this road to make a lasting impression. Keep the camera for a parked stop. The best part of the Grade deserves your eyes.
survey: Two-lane rural highway with agricultural entrances and little shoulder under the trees. Plan fuel before the crossing. Confirm a paved pull-in before stopping a low car.

title: Talbot Islands Passage
sequence: Heckscher Drive at the Fort George ferry landing
description: Start on the north side of the ferry at Fort George. Heckscher Drive runs from salt marsh to island, and the bridge over Nassau Sound gives you the coast in one uninterrupted sweep. Amelia Island brings the trees back before Fernandina Beach marks the finish. Big Talbot is the stop for anyone who brought a camera.
survey: This leg starts beyond the ferry. Allow extra time if approaching from Mayport. Check park hours for a Boneyard Beach stop and expect cyclists on the island sections.

title: Halifax Beachline
sequence: Ocean Shore Boulevard at Granada, Ormond Beach
description: Ponce Inlet starts quietly. Then the towers get taller, the crosswalks get closer and Daytona announces itself without needing a sign. Stay on the paved beachside road through to Granada Boulevard in Ormond Beach. Save this one for a club arrival when half the fun is watching the line of cars roll in.
survey: Busy social Cruise on paved streets. Major Daytona events can change traffic and parking. Driving on the beach is outside this route.

title: Seven Mile Blue
sequence: Big Pine Key at Sands Road
description: Marathon gives you one last run of storefronts before the land falls away. On the Seven Mile Bridge the old rail alignment keeps you company across water that changes color with the clouds. Bahia Honda brings back palms and a place to stretch your legs. The finish is on Big Pine, where the Key deer set the pace.
survey: Fuel and regroup in Marathon before the bridge. Photography belongs at a legal stop such as Bahia Honda. Watch for Key deer on Big Pine, especially around dawn and dusk.

title: Lower Keys to Mile Zero
sequence: US 1 at Sands Road on Big Pine Key
description: The Lower Keys narrow the world to water, mangroves and the red lights of the car ahead. Past Stock Island, the road becomes a city street. Follow it into Old Town until there are no mile markers left to count. Whitehead and Fleming is the finish. Arrange parking first so the crew can enjoy Mile Zero on foot.
survey: Key deer habitat, town traffic and very limited curb space at the finish. North Pine Channel bridge works are a planning consideration. Check FL511 before starting.

title: Santa Rosa Dune Run
sequence: J. Earle Bowden Way east of Pensacola Beach
description: The buildings stop, the dunes turn almost white and the road keeps going between two bodies of water. J. Earle Bowden Way is the Panhandle drive to save for a clear day. Opal Beach gives the crew a chance to step out between the dunes before the Navarre skyline comes back into view.
survey: Wind can blow sand across the pavement. The national seashore can restrict access after storms. Check park alerts, especially with a low front splitter.

title: St. George Island Crossing
sequence: Island Drive at Patton Drive, Eastpoint
East Gulf Beach Drive toward the state park
description: Eastpoint drops behind on the long crossing to St. George Island. The lighthouse marks the change from bridge to beach town. Turn east and the houses start to thin as the road heads toward the state park. Plan the lighthouse stop for after you park. It makes a better crew photo than any shot through a windshield.
survey: Exposed bridge and beach traffic. Park entry, visitor hours and fees apply if you continue into the state park. Plan the return over the same bridge.

title: Cedar Key Landfall
description: Head southwest from Otter Creek. The pines go on long enough to make the first tidal channel feel like a reveal. Then come the short bridges, the first houses on pilings and Cedar Key's little street grid. Second Street is the finish. Give the island the rest of the afternoon and find the waterfront on foot.
survey: Fuel before the rural leg. Low approaches can flood and storm recovery can affect island access. Check local notices before committing to the single main road into town.

title: Ozello Trail
sequence: North Ozello Trail at West Sanddollar Lane
description: Ozello is where Florida puts the bends. The trail threads little pieces of high ground and keeps changing direction as the tidal creeks get in the way. Rooflines, mangroves and open marsh take turns in the windshield. Finish at Sanddollar Lane, then take the same road back and notice how different the corners look.
survey: Dead-end coastal approach with homes, blind bends and little shoulder. High water can cover the low spots. Arrange an off-road turnaround. Give oncoming trucks and trailers room.

title: Sunshine Skyway
description: Begin at the north rest area with Tampa Bay spread out below the windshield. The yellow cables get taller until the deck crests, and for a moment the far shore disappears. Roll down the south side and regroup off the highway. The rest areas give you the angle for a bridge photograph you cannot get from the deck.
survey: Check FL511 for wind restrictions or closures. Account for tolls on the I-275 approach. Both meetup points are off the through lanes. Never stop on the bridge deck.

title: Sanibel Island Arrival
description: Take McGregor toward the water and the mainland lets go in stages. A bridge, a little sweep of island, then another span carries you over San Carlos Bay. Periwinkle Way is the handoff to Sanibel's seriously unhurried streets. Set a meetup on the island so nobody has to chase a gap across the causeway.
survey: The island-bound approach is tolled. Check LeeWay and local causeway access before leaving. Expect cyclists and queues at Periwinkle Way.

title: Flamingo at the End of the Road
sequence: Guy Bradley Visitor Center at Flamingo
description: From the Coe visitor center, the road runs straight into a sea of grass. A patch of trees on the horizon becomes a hardwood hammock, then the landscape opens again. Keep going until the trees give way to mangroves and the pavement meets Florida Bay. Flamingo feels a long way from Miami. Budget for every mile back.
survey: National park entrance requirements apply. Fill up before entering, carry water and save the route for patchy reception. This distance is one way. Stops and the return to Homestead need separate time.

title: Big Cypress Tamiami Trail
description: Ochopee barely interrupts the Tamiami Trail. East of town the cypress trunks stand in dark water and the clearings get wider as the road approaches Shark Valley. Oasis is the place to park and get a close look at the water beside the highway. The club route stays on paved US 41 all the way across.
survey: Bring fuel and an offline backup. The adjoining Loop Road is substantially gravel. Give wildlife space, park clear of the highway and allow extra time if visiting Shark Valley.

title: Biscayne Skyline
sequence: Rickenbacker Causeway by the Virginia Key approach
Bill Baggs Cape Florida State Park
description: The first stretch looks back at a wall of Miami glass. Then Virginia Key and Crandon replace the skyline with palms, and the boulevard settles into island time. Drive to Cape Florida for the finish and walk the last stretch toward the lighthouse if the park is open. Few city drives change character this completely.
survey: The mainland causeway entry is tolled. Check park admission and hours for the finish. Share the crossing with cyclists and allow space around the beach access lanes.

title: Lake Okeechobee East Shore
description: Leave Pahokee beside the great rim of Lake Okeechobee. Through town the road feels local, then Conners Highway turns north and the fields stretch out almost without interruption. The big lake stays hidden behind the dike for much of the drive. Make Port Mayaca the place to get out and look for the water.
survey: Farm vehicles use the same highway. This route stays on US 441 to the SR 76 junction. The dike and lock are separate accesses. Verify public entry before making a photo stop.

title: Palm Beach Ocean Drive
sequence: Lake Avenue at the Lake Worth Beach approach
Ocean Boulevard near Chilean Avenue, Palm Beach
description: Turn north at Lake Worth Beach and follow South Ocean Boulevard up the island. At times the Atlantic is right beside the car. At others, palms and clipped hedges take over. Finish near Chilean Avenue and park before heading toward Worth Avenue. This one works best as a slow arrival with a dinner reservation waiting.
survey: Residential streets, beach crossings and limited public parking. Respect signed restrictions on stopping. The mapped drive runs north along the island.

title: Sebring Race Day Arrival
sequence: US 98 at the Haywood Taylor approach
description: This is Sebring in miniature. Turn off US 98 and follow Haywood Taylor toward the place where endurance teams come to see what twelve hours can break. The public approach ends at Midway Drive. From there the day's ticket and event signs decide where the cars go. Save this short Cruise for an actual race-week arrival.
survey: Public-road approach only. Gates, spectator parking and admission depend on the event. Follow the organizer's arrival instructions if they differ from this preview.

title: Miccosukee Canopy
sequence: Miccosukee Road east of Capital Circle
Miccosukee Road east of the greenway trailheads
description: East of Capital Circle, the oaks lean over Miccosukee Road until the two sides meet. Sun cuts through in little strips across the hood. Take this as a short chapter of Tallahassee's canopy country and get out at a marked greenway entrance if the crew wants photographs under the trees.
survey: Narrow shaded road, greenway users and local driveways. The mapped segment ends on the paved western corridor. Use a legal pull-in for turning or regrouping.

title: Matanzas Inlet
description: Head north from Marineland with the dune line close to the passenger window. Matanzas Inlet opens in a burst of water and marsh on the crossing. Farther up the island, Crescent Beach brings the cafés and crossings back. Save time for the fort area. The stop is on foot and the fort itself is across the water.
survey: Check National Park Service hours and ferry availability if visiting the fort. Beach accesses attract turning traffic. Plan to park before photographing the inlet.

title: Venetian Bay Arrival
sequence: Gulf Shore Boulevard North on the Moorings side of Park Shore
description: Naples gives this one an easy brief. Put the cars together, roll up Gulf Shore Boulevard and arrive at Venetian Bay while there is still color in the water. The drive is deliberately short. The payoff is the line of cars, the waterfront tables and the photographs after everyone has parked.
survey: Short low-speed social arrival. Waterfront and residential parking can be restricted. Arrange a legal meetup space in advance and keep building entrances clear.

title: South Beach Causeway
description: Leave downtown Miami with the towers tight around the car. The MacArthur opens the frame in one move, with the port to one side and islands on the other. South Beach puts you back into the city at walking pace. Park near South Pointe and let the cruise ships provide the final shot.
survey: Urban causeway with commuter and port traffic. South Pointe parking is limited. Plan for event restrictions and a slow final mile through Miami Beach.

title: Launch Coast
description: Start on the Indian River and climb the Max Brewer bridge with the space coast spread out ahead. The road crosses marshland before swinging east to the dunes at Playalinda. On an ordinary day the Atlantic is enough of a finish. On a launch day the space program gets the final say over where the road ends.
survey: Check Canaveral National Seashore alerts before departure. Launch operations, gates and parking limits can cut the drive short. Park admission applies. Keep to the paved visitor road.

title: Suwannee Northbound
sequence: US 41 at Bridge Street, White Springs
description: White Springs is the kind of start where you should hear the river before you hear the engines. From the Bridge Street junction, take US 41 northwest out of town. The Suwannee falls behind and long pine-lined stretches carry the drive into Jasper. Come early for a separate riverside stop at Stephen Foster before starting the run.
survey: Fuel and regroup in town. Rural junctions and wildlife deserve particular care around dawn and dusk. The state park visit is separate from the mapped mileage.
